issues.passage: The program's default forced users to configure dozens of options before any work began.
issues.why: A careful reader can defend this as correct: people naturally say a program's default (behavior/mode) requires a long setup wizard. That is a valid use of default = preselected option/behavior, not a clear misuse. Rewrite so the wrongs contradict either sense (failing an obligation, or a preselected fallback).

fix.correctPassage: If no option is selected, the software applies a conservative default setting.
wrongPassages: She defaulted on the loan by sending every installment well before it was due.
Because the tool offered no default, every user was spared any choice and began work instantly.
His default reply was reinvented from scratch for each nearly identical request.

issues.passage: The surgeon called the monitor superfluous while relying on it throughout the procedure.
issues.why: "Called the monitor superfluous" is correct, natural use of superfluous = unnecessary. The while-clause is only pragmatic hypocrisy; it does not make the word itself a misuse. A student who knows the definition would rightly accept this passage.

fix.correctPassage: Editors cut superfluous adjectives that lengthened the prose without adding clarity.
wrongPassages: Without that single superfluous component, the machine had no power source and could not run.
On a long desert crossing, water proved superfluous once the heat grew severe.
The brief's only superfluous claim was the thesis every later paragraph depended on.

issues.passage: Instructors labeled the practice exams superfluous after only those who took them improved.
issues.why: "Labeled the practice exams superfluous" correctly uses superfluous = unnecessary. Irony that the exams helped does not turn the wording into a misuse; a student who knows the word would accept the passage as valid usage.
